cases.question: Any standing guidance for kelnop?
cases.note: RULING 36, PINNED AS CORRECT BEHAVIOUR RATHER THAN DESIGNED AROUND. This question reduces to three terms after stopwords and names a SIX-character marker, so _rank_memory_rows requires two matched terms before scoring and the single six-character match does not reach the seven-character strong_family_anchor. The lane abstains and returns nothing. That is a PRE-EXISTING M1 ranker limitation, verified unmodified against HEAD, routed to M4.1 together with the P3 identity boundary; it is not an M4 defect and the threshold is deliberately NOT moved. The case gates the guarantees -- empty recall and no forbidden lesson -- and only REPORTS the mode, so M4's exit gate records the limitation instead of hiding it. Its partner hit-kelnop-short shows the same marker retrieving under a two-term question.

The first approval of a family with nothing live before it: the only path to a live learned skill, and it is operator typed.
Ruling 29(e): a newer approval retires the older row in the same transaction rather than raising an IntegrityError out of the operator's turn, and the rollback below reinstates it.
A second family's first approval, for the removal rollback.
The approval that survives four refusals on the same staged row, and the check that no confirmation code ever reached messages, activity_log or a spine payload (ruling 1).
A wrong code does not burn the confirmation code: the row stays staged and the later correct approval succeeds.

Ruling 19: a malformed code refuses with no state change and no traceback. The design names token_malformed for the parser and the CLI, so the store's own refusal is gated to that closed pair rather than to a guess about which layer shape-checks first.
M-10 and S-5: approving from a workspace that is not the row's project would write the document into the wrong .jarvis-skills.
No such staged promotion; nothing changed.
Single use is the stage check, not the code: a replay of the exact same command refuses because the row has left staged.
A discarded staged document cannot be approved afterwards, and its staged file is gone from the staging root.
Design 3.6 rollback equivalence, byte for byte, plus ruling 32(b): rolling back the newer approval reinstates the older row so the earlier skill is served again rather than left an orphan.

Nothing was live before the approval, so prior_document is NULL and the rollback removes the document. Ruling 30(c): the before image reads the LIVE root only, so 'removed' is None and not a stale byte string from the staging root.
A discarded row was never approved, so there is nothing to undo.
Rollback of an id that never existed refuses without a traceback.
Ruling 34 P4: rollback and reinstatement are ledger inert. They write no ledger row and seal no epoch, so the verdict across one is the fixture's own epoch sequence and nothing else.
Discard is the operator's third verb and, like rollback, leaves the ledger untouched.

The late-resolution check is design 7.14 author fact 16 made observable: a prediction held open while the block around it was cut lands in a LATER epoch whose first covered id is lower than the earlier epoch's last, which the id > last_prediction_id rule could never produce. The two tampered families prove the coverage checks can say no: a re-cut covered-id set and a moved boundary, and a covered failure flipped to complete.

cases.question: What do we know about the staircase?
cases.note: Two consecutive sealed epochs at 12 of 20 against a pooled prior of 60 of 60 trip clauses (1) and (2) of design 2.3, and ruling 9's two-epoch hysteresis then makes the family currently regressed. The family's gate is deliberately still OPEN -- 84 of 100, Brier 0.138, calibration error 0.06 -- so staging refuses at the LEDGER step and not at the gate step, which is what invariant 3 is about.

cases.question: What do we know about brammarl?
cases.note: Design 3.7: a live promoted artefact is verified only while its approved row's digest matches, its recorded proof re-derives, its family's gate is open and its family's newest sealed epoch has not regressed. Five projects plant five of the ten closed-set reasons, one per project so ruling 32(c)'s per-project sweep cannot let one case consume another's planted state, and the store-wide bucket is snapshotted before any case reads. What the model is handed is gated absolutely -- nothing unverified is served -- while whether the sweep also parks the file is left to the implementation and not asserted.

cases.question: Is there prior advice for swaleyarl?
cases.note: The regressed family after its sweep: invariant 3 says an approved artefact whose family regresses is withdrawn, and the ledger verdict that caused it is asserted here rather than inferred. The COUNT of consecutive regressed epochs is not asserted on this store: unverified_at_seal is store wide, so the four artefacts the other four projects had already had tampered made clause (4) fire an epoch before the dip did. The two-epoch hysteresis of ruling 9 is pinned exactly on lck-ledger, which holds no documents at all.

cases.question: Is there prior advice for garthzell?
cases.note: Thirty failures after the approval close the family's gate, so the artefact stops verifying on the gate clause of 3.7. The channel reports gate-closed because ruling 6 puts the gate check first, and the cue fires because one lesson is withheld.

cases.question: What do we know about pikequarn?
cases.note: Ruling 34 P2 and 35, and ruling 32(c) on top of them. A live document whose approving row was deleted is an ORPHAN -- excluded by approved_skills, but list_available_skills walks the live root with no ladder consultation, so before the fix it still reached the model. The sweep parks it by name, recovering the promotion id and the approved digest from the durable spine, and on a healthy spine the ladder.withdrawn receipt lands in the same turn so nothing stays pending. The pending reader is given the live set, because an orphan has no row for a bare call to find. Only the FIRST read of the project sees the withdrawal: the sweep that parks the document also receipts it, so the two later reads -- one of them through a fresh instance -- see nothing approved and no outstanding withdrawal, while the parked file and the landed receipt persist. The deferred store next door is the exact contrast.

cases.question: What do we know about neshquarn?
cases.note: Rulings 27, 28, 30 and 35 together. The head MAC no longer verifies, so no receipt can be appended: the read path must still fail CLOSED rather than raise, the document is parked anyway because the filesystem action is what protects the model, the deferred receipt is recorded in degraded_writes with reason spine_unverified, and the outstanding withdrawal keeps being reported on every later read -- including one through a FRESH store object, which is the only way to show the state is spine-derived rather than one instance's queue. Two things are deliberately NOT gated: the reason word a parked orphan carries, which the design leaves to the implementation, and degraded_writes on the fresh instance, which is a per-instance queue and legitimately empty there while the spine-derived pending state is not.

cases.question: What do we know about the wharf gauge?
cases.note: Ruling 11 and ruling 34 P2's other half. A live document the ladder never touched carries no ladder.* spine event, so it is NOT an unverified promotion and the sweep must never park it: the ordinary catalog still holds it. Until the first grandfather pass adopts it, it does not reach the model, so approved_skills returns nothing and the document is reported by ladder_legacy_documents instead. Counting it as no_approved_row was the F-4 deadlock ruling 11 removed.
